source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New York's entire published data center capacity is 3 MW, from one CyrusOne facility in Wappingers Falls, which says more about disclosure than about the state's actual grid load.

The facility publishes 3 MW of IT capacity and 100,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that load is roughly 75 racks. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so what actually runs inside is not documented.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers audited controls for hosting services, not any AI-specific requirement. Nothing published addresses liquid cooling, high-density power delivery, or the substation and interconnection arrangements that decide whether AI accelerators could run at the site. On the record available, this is general colocation space, and AI use of it is unconfirmed.

The state ranking is an artifact of the data, not the buildout. This is the only facility in New York with a published megawatt figure, out of 31 mapped facilities, so its 3 MW is the whole published total for the state. The mapped footprint is far larger than the disclosed capacity, and the gap between them is the real story: capacity that exists but is not reported cannot be counted against the grid.
